summary: FY2025/26 (May 2025–Apr 2026) field yields up in every field but 09A (Agro Table 15, 17.12 t/ha); but May 2026 fell to 1.14 t/ha from 1.40, with falls in 05A, 06A, 16A, 19A and 05D (Agro).
FY2025/26 (May 2025–Apr 2026) crop 22,111 t, 16.90 t/ha vs 20.63 budget (-18% on tonnes); Main Division 19.49 t/ha, Tobe/Sg Kaindangan only 12.13 vs 22.07 budget (PA).
Cost RM375.83/t vs RM325.05 budget (+16%), mainly from the low crop; roads RM873/ha, pruning RM255/ha and drains RM76/ha over budget (PA).
Very wet year (4,122 mm, 780 and 870 mm in Jan–Feb 2026) delayed manuring, weeding and Tobe harvesting; FY2025/26 manuring only finished in May 2026 (Agro).

issues.title: FY2025/26 yield: 16.90 (PA) vs 17.12 t/ha (Agro)
issues.detail: PA Table 19 / 8.2: 22,111.368 t on 1,308.31 ha = 16.90 t/ha, prior year 16.49 t/ha (13,632.529 t on 826.72 ha, Main Division only). Agro Table 15: FY25/26 17.12 t/ha vs FY24/25 16.35 t/ha (+4%). The PA divides by 1,308.31 ha, the old mature area, although its own area statement now gives mature 1,267.32 ha (on 1,267.32 ha the yield would be 17.45). Neither report states the Agro hectare basis.

issues.title: PA: yield '14% below budget' is 18%
issues.detail: PA 8.2 and 13.11: 16.90 t/ha is '14% below the budgeted amount of 20.63 tons'. (20.63 - 16.90) / 20.63 = 18% below, the same as the 18% FFB shortfall (22,111.368 vs 26,990 t) on the same 1,308.31 ha.

issues.title: Agro yield % columns use the wrong base
issues.detail: Agro Tables 15 and 16 divide the change by the NEW year, not the old. Table 16: total 1.40 to 1.14 t/ha is printed -23% (actual -19%); 05A 1.33 to 0.71 printed -87% (actual -47%); 06A -62% (actual -38%); 19A -50% (actual -33%); 16A -57% (actual -36%); 10B 0.36 to 1.17 printed +69% (actual +225%). Table 15: 19A 11.69 to 18.49 printed +37% (actual +58%); total +4% (actual +5%). Text 8.8 repeats the 23% decline.

issues.title: Mature/immature split: PA 1,267.32/80.01 vs Agro 1,296.76/50.57 ha
issues.detail: Both give planted 1,347.33 ha. PA Table 1 (Apr 2026): mature 1,267.32, immature 80.01 (23A 63.46 + 24A 8.74 + 25A 7.81). Agro Table 1: mature 1,296.76, immature 50.57, saying 23A04 was moved to mature. But 50.57 = 24A 8.74 + 25A 7.81 + 34.02, which is 23A4's own area, so the immature total still contains 23A4 and the sub-block named in the text cannot be right (23A5 is 29.40 ha). Agro section 7 heading also says 23A-34.02 ha while 7.2 says 23A 33.02 ha; PA 13.13 says 62.46 ha vs 63.46 in PA Table 2. Gross area: PA 1,492.34 ha title vs Agro 1,524.67 ha.

issues.title: Pruning progress: PA 115% vs Agro 69–99%
issues.detail: Same FY2025/26 programme (e.g. 04A 86,032 palms) but different actuals. PA Table 13: 04A 105,496 (123%), 08A 25,349 (86%), 10A 55,638 (89%), 16A 66,386 (90%), total 749,037 of 650,264 = 115%, 4.6 rounds. Agro Table 8/11 (to May 2026): 04A 84,898 (99%), 08A 20,369 (69%), 10A 43,882 (70%), 10B 31,037 (93%), 16A 52,202 (71%); Agro says Tobe pruning was not completed as scheduled while PA 6.4.2 says the work was completed.

issues.title: FY2025/26 manuring tonnage and % differ
issues.detail: PA Table 10 (to Apr 2026): programme 1,441.17 t, applied 1,097.72 t = 76%. Agro Table 5 (to May 2026): programme Mix A 524.05 + Mix B 217.25 + Mix C 490.40 + RP 231.90 + CPD 5.15 = 1,468.75 t (PA: Mix A 540.15, Mix B 185.91, Mix C 488.71, RP 226.40). Agro prints 100% completion for every line, but its own applied column shows Mix A 429.52 of 524.05 (82%) and Mix B 152.55 of 217.25 (70%), total 1,301.19 t (89%).

issues.title: Weeding progress: PA vs Agro per field
issues.detail: Tobe fields FY2025/26 selective spray PA Table 9 vs Agro Table 12: 08A 38% vs 33%, 10A 37% vs 33%, 10B 36% vs 31%, 16A 56% vs 52%; circle PA Table 7 vs Agro: 08A 59% vs 55%, 10A 76% vs 92%, 10B 64% vs 56%, 16A 90% vs 84%. Main Division: 05A selective PA 67% vs Agro 160%; 09A PA 311% (199.30 ha on 21.38 ha, 9.3 rounds) vs Agro 106%. The PA 09A row looks like a data-entry error.

issues.title: PA spraying tables use wrong field rows and total area
issues.detail: PA Tables 7 and 9 total 1,370.08 ha (planted area is 1,347.33) and list fields '2024A 17.37 ha', '2003A 68.84 ha' and a second '2005A 7.81 ha', which look like old labels for 23A/24A/25A. Circle completed column sums to 2,841.05 (printed 2,841.1); selective sums to 2,586.48 (printed 2,586.68). Text 6.1.3.1 prints the programme as '4,10.24' ha (should be 4,110.24).

issues.title: Immature area change described wrongly
issues.detail: PA 2.2: 'The immature area had reduced from 56.39 hectares to 80.01 hectares, a reduction of 5.38 hectares'. 56.39 to 80.01 is an increase of 23.62 ha.

issues.title: Palm census totals do not add
issues.detail: Agro Table 3: previous palms printed 163,770 but rows sum to 168,904; current printed 170,356 but rows sum to 172,422. Previous hectares 1,400.72 (rows) vs current 1,347.29. 04A shows 21,993 palms while PA Table 13 uses 21,508. PA Table 2 SPH also differs from the Agro census: 2025A 81 vs 126, 2024A 119 vs 124, 2016A 122 vs 126, 2010B 114 vs 117.

issues.title: Harvesting round averages and ranges inconsistent
issues.detail: PA Table 16 total prints 2.85 rounds in Feb 2026 and 28.5 rounds to date (7.11), but the block rows average about 2.0 rounds a month and 22.2 rounds to date. PA 7.12–7.13 say rates RM41–56/t, output 0.50–2.83 t/man-day and income RM35–118/day, while Table 17 shows rates RM41–61/t, output 0.44–4.09 t and income RM20.24–188.14/day. 7.10 calls the 18–19 rounds '18 to 19 days'.

issues.title: General charges: RM2,237,941 vs RM2,102,569
issues.detail: PA Table 5 and Appendix 1 total general charges RM2,237,941 (RM1,628/ha on 1,374.51 ha). The cost of production Table 20 uses RM2,102,569 (RM95.09/t), described in Appendix 1 as the proportion to mature area. On the full amount it would be about RM101.21/t and the total cost about RM381.95/t. The hectare basis (1,374.51 ha) is also different from the crop table (1,308.31) and area statement (1,267.32).

issues.title: Dates, names and units
issues.detail: PA 1.1 says the previous visit was 21–22 October 2026 (after this April 2026 visit; presumably 2025), and PA 4.1 calls it September 2025. PA 5.1 and Table 6 say financial year 2026/26 (should be 2025/26); PA page header says (2-2025). Estate Manager is Mr Mark Mathew in the PA but Mr Mark Anderson in the Agro report. PA 6.6.1 says the drain budget was 8,500 chains while Table 15 is in metres and 6.6.3 converts 3,478 m to 173 chains. PA 6.2.7 gives manuring income RM51.80 'per hectare' (should be per man-day). PA 6.1.1 says 29 maintenance workers, then 17 deployed to Kaindangan and 19 to the Main Division (36).

issues.title: Agro Appendix 1(C) areas differ from Agro Table 2
issues.detail: FY26/27 fertiliser programme Appendix 1(C) (titled 'Tobe Division - Immature' but listing mature fields 08A–16A and Main Division field 09A/block 80) uses old areas: 08A blocks 82–83 63.34 ha vs Table 2 59.33; 10A+10B blocks 84–91 235.25 vs 209.22; 16A blocks 92–99 163.60 vs 150.67; 23A A4+A5 68.84 vs 63.42. Appendix 1(B) labels field 25A as '2025B'. Fertiliser tonnages built on these areas would be overstated.

issues.title: 'Last year' crop column is Main Division only
issues.detail: PA Table 19 'Tanjung Nipis Total Estate' last-year column (13,632.529 t, 826.72 ha, 16.49 t/ha) is identical to the Main Division row; Sg Kaindangan (Tobe) is excluded. kpi.yphPrevSame 16.49 and the FY2024/25 tonnage are therefore not like-for-like with FY2025/26 (22,111.368 t, 1,308.31 ha). Main Division alone: 13,632.529 t to 16,526.865 t (16.49 to 19.49 t/ha).

kb:
TANJUNG NIPIS ESTATE (TNE), Meridian Plantations Sdn Bhd, United Malacca Berhad (UMB) group. The estate has a Main Division and the Sg. Kaindangan Estate, also called the Tobe Division, which was acquired last year after long neglect and has been rehabilitated. Fact pack from PA Report 01/2026 (Planting Advisor En. Adnan Bin Mustafa; visit 27-28 April 2026; review period May 2025 to April 2026, 12 months, financial year FY2025/26 runs May to April) and Agronomy Advisory Report 1/2026 (Junior Agronomist Mr Alison Bin Janari and Senior Agronomist Mr Chong Kuan Ming; visit 25 May 2026; previous Agro visit 28 November 2025; manuring programme 2026). Senior (Regional) Manager Mr Phor Kok Beng. Estate Manager Mr Mark Mathew per PA (Agro: Mr Mark Anderson). PA says its previous visit was 21-22 October 2026 (typo). FFB goes to Paitan Palm Oil Mill.

AREA (PA Table 1 and 2, April 2026, after a GIS census): estate title 1,492.34 ha. Planted 1,347.33 ha (90% of title): mature 1,267.32 ha (down 40.99 ha from 1,308.31), immature 80.01 ha, replanting 0. Roads 85.36, unplantable 28.08, ponds 1.88, swamps/forest 21.40, river/drain/buffer 1.45, buildings/others 6.84 (Table 2: 6.30 plus land dispute 0.54). Mature fields (ha, SPH): 2004A 162.96 (132), 2005A 35.63 (119), 2005B 158.28 (133), 2005C 115.54 (131), 2005D 202.38 (141), 2006A 70.99 (124), 2009A 21.38 (111), 2019A 80.94 (139), 2008A 59.33 (124), 2010A 136.10 (115), 2010B 73.12 (114), 2016A 150.67 (122). Immature: 2023A 63.46 ha (Sg Kaindangan blocks 23A4 34.02 and 23A5 29.44), 2024A 8.74 (119 SPH), 2025A 7.81 (81 SPH). The former field 2023A in the Main Division was split into 2024A6 (8.74 ha) and 2025A7 (7.81 ha).
Agronomy Table 1: mature 1,296.76, immature 50.57, planted 1,347.33 (88% of gross 1,524.67 ha); field road 121.45, roads 16.78, swamps/forest 18.84, unplanted 12.37. Agro says mature increased after Block 23A04 was reclassified as mature. Agro blocking adjustments in Tobe fields P08A, P10A, P16A and P24A after GIS verification. Tobe area is 539.10 ha per Agro section 5 heading.
Palm census (Agro Table 3, previous vs current SPH): 08A 116 to 126 (+8%), 10A 102 to 115 (+11%), 10B 104 to 117 (+11%), 16A 109 to 126 (+13%), 23A 56 to 102 (+45%, census in progress), 24A 89 to 124 (+28%), 25A 128 to 126; other fields unchanged (04A 135, 05A 119, 05B 133, 05C 131, 05D 141, 06A 124, 09A 111, 19A 139). Increases due to better access for counting and supplying in 23A. 23A at 102 SPH is below standard; vacant areas in 23A-05 need supplementary planting.
Age profile (Agro): 55% (745.78 ha) aged 20-25 years versus ideal 24%; 39% (521.54 ha) 8-19 years prime age; 6% (79.97 ha) 0-3 years; none 4-7 years.
Replanting (Agro Table 4, updated 10 June 2026): 2005 blocks 63 (27.4 ha, 129 SPH), 64 (27.2 ha, 149 SPH) and 65 (54.2 ha, 145 SPH), total 108.7 ha, felling May 2027 (FY27/28), palm age 22, IOI seed. Yields FY22/23 to FY25/26: block 63 20.53, 16.30, 14.00, 16.31; block 64 15.07, 13.48, 13.27, 17.02; block 65 8.41, 11.88, 10.92, 14.67 t/ha. Chosen because of steep land and improper terracing limiting access; Agro agrees.

STAFF (PA section 3, April 2026): Estate Manager Mark Mathew (E12, joined 14/9/2024); Assistant Managers Erikly Effyfian Meyrick (E9, Sg Kaindangan/Tobe, from 17/2/2025) and Alexander Gaya (E8, Main Division); 1 chief clerk, 4 field conductors, 2 clerks (new store clerk from 1/3/2026). Complement sufficient.

LABOUR (PA Table 4, April 2026): 130 workers vs 133 required (7 local, 115 Indonesian, 8 Filipino; no contractors), 6 fewer than at last visit; 1 worker per 10 ha. Harvesters 80 vs 84 required (2 fewer than last visit), 1 per 16 ha, in 3 gangs (1 Sg Kaindangan, 2 Main). Sprayers 9 (req 10), manuring 11 (req 10), FFB loaders 2 (req 4), security 5 (req 4). PA 6.1.1: 29 maintenance workers at the visit including 9 new recruits not yet in the statement; labour for manuring rose from 19 to 29.

CROP (PA Table 19, FY2025/26, May 2025 to April 2026): estate 22,111.368 t vs budget 26,990 t (-18%), 1,308.31 ha, 16.90 t/ha vs 20.63 budget (PA prints -14%; arithmetic -18%); last year same period 13,632.529 t, 826.72 ha, 16.49 t/ha (Main Division only). Main Division 16,526.865 t vs 16,831 (-2%), 848.10 ha, 19.49 t/ha vs 19.85. Kaindangan (Tobe) 5,584.503 t vs 10,159 budget (-45%), 460.21 ha, 12.13 t/ha vs 22.07.
Agronomy Table 15 (Period 12, full year): FY24/25 vs FY25/26 t/ha: 04A 17.79 to 21.44; 05A 10.83 to 13.47; 05B 17.72 to 23.28; 05C 15.03 to 17.84; 05D 13.41 to 17.58; 06A 17.71 to 20.10; 08A 0 to 12.67; 09A 15.51 to 15.18; 10A 0 to 10.95; 10B 0 to 9.92; 16A 0 to 15.45; 19A 11.69 to 18.49; total 16.35 to 17.12 (+4% as printed). 04A, 05B, 06A near potential; 05A, 05C, 05D, 09A below expected level. Tobe fields acceptable for their recovery stage; their FY24/25 0 means not yet under the estate. Dashboard block yields use this table (FY2025/26, prevYtd = FY2024/25); May 2026 figures are in block notes.
Agronomy Table 16 (Period 1 = May): FY25/26 vs FY26/27 t/ha: 04A 2.13 to 1.77; 05A 1.33 to 0.71; 05B 1.70 to 1.31; 05C 0.98 to 1.37; 05D 1.59 to 1.14; 06A 1.80 to 1.11; 08A 0.84 to 1.08; 09A 1.68 to 1.36; 10A 0.67 to 1.08; 10B 0.36 to 1.17; 16A 1.21 to 0.77; 19A 1.57 to 1.05; 23A 0 to 0.08; total 1.40 to 1.14 (printed -23%; arithmetic gives -19%). Causes given: FY25/26 manuring finished only in May 2026 and FY26/27 not started; long Tobe intervals; incomplete weeding; recovering palms; Mg deficiency in 19A.

COST OF PRODUCTION (PA Table 20, FY2025/26 12 months, RM per tonne FFB on 22,111 t actual and 26,990 t budget): general charges RM2,102,569 = RM95.09/t (budget RM2,125,546 = 78.75); upkeep and cultivation RM3,496,857 = 158.15 (budget 3,798,398 = 140.73); harvesting and collection RM2,710,651 = 122.59 (budget 2,849,381 = 105.57); total RM8,310,077 = RM375.83/t vs RM8,773,325 = RM325.05/t budget, 16% over, mainly because crop was 18% under budget. PA: cost reasonable.

GENERAL CHARGES (PA Table 5 and Appendix 1, on 1,374.51 ha actual / 1,414.10 budget): total RM2,237,941 = RM1,628/ha vs RM2,280,993 = RM1,613/ha (+1%). Staff salary and related RM689,353 (RM502/ha vs 539); labour overhead RM576,000 (419 vs 455); office related RM850,757 (619 vs 564, +10%); office and premises upkeep RM121,831 (89 vs 55, +62%). Overspends over 10%: staff accommodation +RM1,833 (46%); lines electricity and water +RM1,867 (75%, unbudgeted backhoe); non-capitalised fixed asset +RM13,186 (950%); cess/rate/rent +RM5,739 (11%, quit rent); computer maintenance +RM2,528 (21%, Lyntramax fees); entertainment/foods +RM6,925 (98%, MLP charges for GIS and IAD visits, NBES); security +RM16,134 (15%, extra Tobe watchman and gate); transport and travelling +RM40,250 (52%, staff trip to Malacca annual dinner); other building maintenance +RM48,006 (148%, Tobe carpenter and workshop, fertiliser store repair, diesel tank calibration). Largest lines: water/electricity RM362,065, staff salary RM457,434, labour paid leave RM176,863, labour recruitment RM135,012 (budget 251,322), security RM125,346, transport RM116,986, labour welfare RM115,235, staff bonus RM106,743. Depreciation RM959,870 and amortisation RM420,417 excluded (total with them RM3,618,228). Cost per staff RM76,595; cost per labour RM4,431 for 130 workers (budget 156).

UPKEEP AND CULTIVATION (PA Table 6, RM/ha actual vs budget): supervision 30 vs 35; weeding 268 vs 231 (RM339,839); manuring 1,148 vs 1,588 (RM1,455,052, low because programme behind); composting 43 vs 0; pests and diseases 45 vs 35; census and thinning 3 vs 9; drains 76 vs 20 (+280%); roads and bridges 873 vs 759 (+15%, RM1,106,070); soil/water conservation 13 vs 53; boundaries 1 vs 1; pruning 255 vs 149 (+71%, corrective pruning in Sg Kaindangan); tools 5 vs 4; total RM2,759/ha vs RM2,883 (RM158/t vs 141).

WEEDING (PA): circle and path spraying 2,841.10 of 4,110.24 ha programme = 69%, 2.1 of 3.0 rounds; interrow selective 2,586.68 ha = 63%, 1.9 rounds, delayed by manuring after heavy rain in Jan-Mar 2026. Circle RM18/ha, 4.5 ha/man-day, RM81/day; interrow RM24/ha, 3.0 ha/man-day, RM72/day (target 4.5 ha); minimum wage RM65.38. Rates rose from RM15 and RM21/ha. Herbicides: Glyphosate for circles; Trichlopyr (Kenlon) and Metsulfuron (Ally 20DF) by mist blower for interrow. Weeds still dominant: Clidemia hirta, Eupatorium, Hedyotis, Melastoma, Asystasia, VOP, Stenochlaena, Bracken, sedges; Lalang, Pennisetum, Giant Paspalum, bamboo grass reduced. Jungle trees poisoned with Trichlopyr successfully.
Agronomy: Main Division only two of three rounds done for both interrow and circle (05A and 09A had three interrow rounds); third round in Mar-Apr 2026 dropped to support manuring. Tobe: one interrow round, about two circle rounds (Table 12: 08A 33%/55%, 10A 33%/92%, 10B 31%/56%, 16A 52%/84%). 19A: circle 3 rounds; interrow 3 rounds in A1 only. FY26/27 weeding not yet started in Main Division. VOP control round planned for FY26/27. Soft grasses and Nephrolepis in blocks 48, 49, 55, 56, 58.

MANURING (PA Table 10, FY2025/26 to April 2026): programme 1,441.17 t, applied 1,097.72 t (76%); first half 873.29 of 902.64 t (97%), second half 224.43 of 538.53 t (42%). Delayed by heavy rain Jan-Mar 2026 and manpower; expected complete May 2026. Mix A 1.5-2.0 kg/palm, RM20/ha, 2.59 ha/man-day, RM51.80/day (low). Buckets used on steep land; PA suggests wheelbarrows, small vehicles and mechanisation; no manuring in Nov-Dec.
Agronomy Table 5: FY2025/26 completed May 2026 (Mix A 524.05 t, Mix B 217.25, Mix C 490.40, RP 231.90, CPD 5.15 programme). Delays: late delivery in second half, weather on hills, Tobe access. FY26/27 (Table 6) first-half programme Mix A 448.9 t, Mix B 414.36, NK1 199.32, AS 30.17, BRP 80.49, CPD 26.9, Aruma 0.13; only Mix A 231.4 t delivered; application to start June 2026. Store satisfactory.
FY26/27 recommendations (Agro Appendix 1, kg/palm): 2004A-2005D Mix A 2.0-2.2 (Jun), NK1 2.0 (Sep), Mix A 2.0-2.2 (Dec), Mix A 2.0 (Mar), BRP 0.75 in some blocks (Jul); 2006A Mix A/NK1 2.0 alternating May, Aug, Nov, Feb; 2019A and 2016 Mix B 2.2 four times plus AS 1.0 and BRP 1.0; 2008-2010 Tobe Mix B 2.0-2.2 four times plus BRP 0.75-1.0; 23A CPD 1.5 thrice, BRP 1.0, Mix B 1.5; 24A and 25A CPD 0.8-1.5 with BRP. Grades: Mix A 9.45:0:24:4; NK1 10.5:0:30; Mix B 9.45:0:24:3.7:0.48; RP 30%; CPD 14:13:9:2.5; Mix C 9.45:0:27:2.7. Agro: no revision needed for FY26/27; to be reviewed at second visit.

PESTS AND DISEASES (PA): rat baiting one round on 1,308.31 ha with STORM (2 baits/palm Main, 1 in Sg Kaindangan), programme complete; STORM dearer than budgeted Ebor so cost RM45/ha vs 35. No bagworm treatment; some signs seen. No Oryctes treatment, no serious damage. Odd Ganoderma palm in 2004/2005 fields; no census. Rat census every 3 months; bait above 10%. Agro: localised rat damage in Tobe and 19A, formal census recommended; RB-damaged palms in 24A/25A not fully recovered.

PRUNING (PA Table 13): 749,037 palms vs 650,264 programme (115%, 4.6 rounds), excess from corrective pruning in Sg Kaindangan, now complete. Fronds to be stacked in patches within 4 palms. Agro (Table 8, to May 2026): Main Division 87-99%; Tobe (Table 11) 08A 69%, 10A 70%, 10B 93%, 16A 71%, short of harvesters; frond snapping on steep hills; FY26/27 cycle started.

ROADS AND DRAINS (PA): grading 873 of 5,927 chains (15%) at RM1.45/m (RM29.18/chain), to finish by June 2026; gravelling 385 chains (92%); 12,416 t crusher run/red stone at RM52.69/t; backhoe 1,001 hours at RM48/hr, excavator 1,962 hours at RM80/hr. Roads RM873/ha vs 759. Drain desilting 4x3x2 ft 3,478 m, 6x4x3 ft 1,608 m, plus 320 m and 590 m in larger sizes; drains RM76/ha vs 20. EFB in Sg Kaindangan (soil conservation RM13/ha); palm base mounding in 2019A1. Boundaries RM1/ha; no FFB theft but security must tighten.

HARVESTING (PA): manual cut and carry with wheelbarrows; mini crawler damaged; farm tractor with grabber loads to bins; external transport outsourced at RM24, 26 and 27/t; internal transport by estate tractors, outsourcing pending contractor consent. Feb 2026 intervals mostly 10-16 days, blocks 48-49 16-21 days; blocks 64, 67, 68, 90 only 1 round. Harvester rates RM41-61/t, output 0.44-4.09 t/man-day. Harvest and collection (Table 18) RM122.59/t vs 105.57: supervision 5.38, harvesting 65.43, loose fruit 0.05, infield loading 7.77 (unbudgeted), ramp 0.25, internal transport 20.34 vs 15.00, tools 1.56, despatch/selling 21.81 vs 20.63; excluding external transport RM100.78 vs 84.95.
Agronomy: Main Division intervals within standard (19A 9-14 days all year; 08A over standard 21-24 days Apr 2026). Tobe intervals worsened from Dec 2025; Apr-May 2026 10B up to 31 days, most Tobe up to 20 days in May. Harvesting rounds May 2026: 04A, 06A, 09A, 19A 3; 05C 2.8; 05D 2.7; 10B 2.5; 05B 2.3; 05A 2; 08A and 10A 1.7 (85%); 16A 1 (50%). Crop quality good; some oxidised loose fruit at platforms.

PALM CONDITION (Agro): no major deficiencies; blocks 52, 65, 68, 67, 54, 80 improving. Etiolation in ravines; no thinning where replanting within 5 years. Tobe palms thin-trunked after under two years of fertiliser; waterlogging in block 85 being drained. 19A A1/A2 suspected magnesium deficiency on sandy hardpan soil; EFB and drains started.

VEHICLES (PA Table 21, to Feb 2026): farm tractors over budget by more than 40% (e.g. Kubota SAC3874E RM26.23/hr vs 13.43) due to repairs; damaged mini crawlers to be written off.

RAINFALL (Agro): FY20/21 3,745 mm/190 days; FY21/22 3,763.5/190; FY22/23 3,432.5/188; FY23/24 2,864/179; FY24/25 4,137/203; FY25/26 4,122/203 (Main Division; Jan 2026 780 mm, Feb 870 mm); May 2026 168 mm/12 days.

IMMATURE (PA): 2024A/2025A planted, supplying needed after floods and monkeys; 23A rehabilitation, terraces done; spray remaining Lalang and bamboo grass, then Garlon and Ally; add drains; GIS stand census. PA concluding: performance improving; focus on interrow weeds, worker productivity and mechanisation; consider package harvesting contract starting with Tobe.
